title: Vesper and the Echo
premise: Astrid Dravenmoor, a clone of the murdered shipping magnate Elias Dravenmoor, has spent three years hiding in the cargo lanes between two hostile fleets. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, both fleets believe the other triggered a weapon, and only Astrid knows the truth: his original's killer, still alive inside the jump-gate authority, is using the flicker to mask a mass theft of gate cores. To prevent a war and expose the killer before the last jump window closes, Astrid must impersonate Elias convincingly enough to hold a fragile truce—a lie that costs him the found family he built on his freighter when they learn he's been deceiving them too. In the end, Astrid testifies as himself, not as Elias, breaking the inheritance of his original's identity; the truce holds, the killer falls into the closing jump window, and Astrid finally claims a name that is entirely his own.
about_author: Zephyrine Dunmore is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who traded flight manifests for fiction after a decade scheduling cargo through contested space. They write character-driven science fiction about people who survive by becoming someone else.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Hauling ore through contested orbits, Astrid feels gravity die for exactly nine seconds—cargo floating, crew screaming, then everything slamming back. The emotional beat: dread, because only one thing could cause it, and it means someone found him.

chapters.title: The Face He Wears
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Astrid's POV: waking in a growth vat three years ago with Elias Dravenmoor's memories and murder case dumped in his head. Emotional beat: grief for a life that was never his, and resolve to stay invisible.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Answer
chapters.summary: POV shifts to engineer Sefa Okonkwo aboard Astrid's freighter, the Long Answer. She patches the gravity-damage and notices Astrid's hands shaking. Emotional beat: warmth—the ragtag crew is the family Astrid never chose but needs, and Sefa senses he's lying about something.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Truce
chapters.summary: Admiral Corvane of the Concord fleet POV. The nine-second flicker reads as a weapons test; her council demands retaliation against the Meridian fleet. Emotional beat: cold calculation masking fear, establishing the war clock ticking toward the jump window.

chapters.title: A Message from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Astrid receives an encrypted transmission addressed to Elias Dravenmoor—sent from inside the jump-gate authority. The sender knows what he is. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into curiosity; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: The Killer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid decodes the message using Elias's memories: gate administrator Veyra Solenne, Elias's murderer, is siphoning gate cores under cover of the flicker. Emotional beat: rage and vertigo as inherited memories become evidence.

chapters.title: What the Crew Deserves
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She confronts Astrid about his shaking hands and locked cabin; he deflects with half-truths. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into hurt—the first crack in the found family, caused by Astrid's secrecy.

chapters.title: Concord Summons
chapters.summary: Concord patrol boards the Long Answer and scans Astrid: genetic match to Elias Dravenmoor, flagged traitor or asset. Admiral Corvane orders him brought in. Emotional beat: claustrophobic panic—invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Wearing the Dead
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, interrogated by Corvane. He makes a devil's bargain: he'll pose as Elias at the truce summit to buy time investigating Solenne. Emotional beat: self-loathing braided with desperate competence—he lies beautifully and hates it.

chapters.title: The Summit of Ashfall Station
chapters.summary: Multi-POV summit scene: Astrid-as-Elias faces both fleets while Solenne watches from the gate delegation, smiling. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; every word risks exposing him or triggering war.

chapters.title: Solenne's Invitation
chapters.summary: Solenne privately greets 'Elias,' revealing she knows he's the clone—and offers him partnership: help her finish the core theft, inherit everything Elias built. Emotional beat: seductive temptation, the inheritance theme weaponized.

chapters.title: Gravity Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid investigates the flicker's source in the gate infrastructure with Sefa, who followed him. They find the second flicker is scheduled—bigger, permanent. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership rekindling trust even as his lie deepens.

chapters.title: The Lie Between Us
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She discovers the clone records and realizes Astrid has been masquerading at the summit as a dead man without telling his own crew. Emotional beat: betrayal—the family fractures exactly when he needs them most.

chapters.title: Corvane's Doubt
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Her intelligence flags inconsistencies in 'Elias,' and she suspects Solenne orchestrated the flicker—but accusing her means admitting the truce rests on a clone's performance. Emotional beat: lonely integrity versus political survival.

chapters.title: Stowaway Evidence
chapters.summary: Young deckhand Pip smuggles a data-slate off Solenne's ship containing the core-theft manifest. Astrid now has proof but no credibility. Emotional beat: fierce hope from the smallest crew member, the found family rallying despite the rift.

chapters.title: The Price of the Mask
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Solenne threatens to reveal his clone status to both fleets unless he delivers the manifest back. He must choose: protect the lie or protect the truth. Emotional beat: crushing weight of survival's cost—his own existence as collateral.

chapters.title: Burning the Original
chapters.summary: Astrid confesses everything to the assembled crew—clone status, the impersonation, the threat. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; he offers them the chance to abandon him, and instead they choose to stand with the man, not the mask.

chapters.title: Second Flicker
chapters.summary: Solenne triggers the permanent gravity collapse early; stations begin drifting, the jump window destabilizing. Multi-POV chaos. Emotional beat: vertiginous urgency—the price of survival is now everyone's to pay.

chapters.title: The Testimony of a Copy
chapters.summary: Astrid broadcasts the manifest and stands before both fleets—not as Elias, but as Astrid Dravenmoor, witness. Emotional beat: defiant self-ownership; the inheritance rejected, the name reclaimed.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: Climax at Vesper Gate: Astrid and Sefa sabotage the core siphon while Corvane arrests Solenne's conspirators. Solenne flees into the collapsing jump window rather than surrender. Emotional beat: breathless action resolving into stunned silence as the window seals behind her.

chapters.title: Gravity Restored
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the truce holds, anchored by Astrid's testimony; Corvane grants the Long Answer a charter under its own name. Emotional beat: quiet relief, grief for what the lie cost, gratitude for who stayed.

chapters.title: A Name That Is Mine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, final chapter. He registers 'Astrid Dravenmoor' legally—first, not second—and the crew throws him a birthday for a date he chooses himself. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging; the echo finally becomes a voice.
